text:
The Buffalo Bills have spent the past month facing opponents without their starting quarterbacks.

Now they could face the Kansas City Chiefs without their starting running back.

The Bills appear to have escaped their 26-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday without any significant new injuries.

Wide receiver DJ Moore briefly left the victory with a knee injury but returned, while defensive tackle Ed Oliver played after unexpectedly landing on the injury report with an oblique injury.

Buffalo (9-1) has won six consecutive games, including four straight against teams starting backup or third-string quarterbacks.

Kenneth Walker III missed Kansas City's 34-7 win against the Arizona Cardinals Sunday with a groin injury, leaving the Chiefs four days to get him ready for their Thanksgiving night matchup against Buffalo.

Kansas City (8-2) played without Walker, starting guard Trey Smith and offensive lineman Jaylon Moore. Tight end Noah Gray and fullback Ben VanSumeren were also injured during the game.

The Bills host the Chiefs at 8:20 p.m. Thursday at Highmark Stadium.

NFL teams have to submit a report on practice participation on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday for a Thursday game. There are three levels of practice participation that can be designated: did not participate, limited participation and full participation.

A game status report is due by 4 p.m. Wednesday for Thursday games.

Here is the Bills vs. Chiefs injury report for Week 12:

Buffalo Bills injury update for Week 12

DJ Moore, WR, knee

DJ Moore provided Buffalo's biggest injury scare Sunday.

The veteran wide receiver landed awkwardly during Josh Allen's interception late in the second quarter against Miami. He limped off the field and headed to the locker room for an examination.

The Bills listed Moore as questionable to return with a knee injury, but he was back on the field for Buffalo's next possession.

Moore caught an 18-yard pass shortly after returning and finished with eight receptions for 91 yards and a touchdown.

Ed Oliver, DL, oblique

Ed Oliver was a surprise addition to Buffalo's injury report Saturday after reporting discomfort in his oblique at the team's facility that morning, according to Syracuse.com's Matt Parrino.

The defensive tackle was listed as questionable against Miami but played Sunday.

Oliver finished with two tackles, including one for a loss. He missed three games earlier this season because of hip and knee injuries.

Christian Benford, CB, groin

Christian Benford missed Sunday's victory over Miami after sitting out all three practices last week.

The starting cornerback suffered a groin injury during Buffalo's Nov. 15 win over the New York Jets.

The Bills elevated former All-Pro cornerback Tre'Davious White from the practice squad for the Miami game. White made his season debut and recorded a pass defended.

Dorian Williams, LB, calf

Dorian Williams did not play Sunday after injuring his calf against the Jets on Nov. 15.

Rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr made his first NFL start against Miami, recording three tackles.

Dalton Kincaid, TE, thumb/ankle

Dalton Kincaid was inactive against Miami after being listed as doubtful with thumb and ankle injuries.

He did not participate in any of Buffalo's three practices last week.

Kincaid had 32 catches for 487 receiving yards and two touchdowns in nine games this season.

T.J. Sanders, DL, shoulder

T.J. Sanders did not play against the Dolphins.

The defensive lineman questionable after being limited in practice Thursday and Friday. He was among Buffalo's seven inactive players Sunday.

Buffalo Bills injured reserve

Joshua Palmer, WR, hamstring

Joshua Palmer was placed on injured reserve Nov. 9 after suffering a hamstring injury during Buffalo's Nov. 1 victory over Baltimore.

Palmer will miss Buffalo's upcoming games against Miami and Kansas City. The earliest Palmer can return is Dec. 6 against the New England Patriots.

Palmer has four receptions for 117 yards and two touchdowns in six games this season.

Zane Durant, DL, neck

Zane Durant began the season on injured reserve because of a neck injury.

He is eligible to return when medically cleared. Buffalo can designate him to return and open his 21-day practice window.

Buffalo Bills non-football injury

Dorian Strong, CB, neck

Kansas City Chiefs injury update for Week 12

Kenneth Walker III, RB, groin

Kenneth Walker III missed Sunday's win over the Arizona Cardinals after being ruled out with a groin injury.

He back did not practice Wednesday, Thursday or Friday last week.

Walker's availability for Thanksgiving is uncertain.

Walker has 872 rushing yards and seven touchdowns on 159 carries and 26 receptions for 172 receiving yards and four touchdowns in eight games.

Trey Smith, G, concussion

Trey Smith did not play against the Cardinals due to a concussion he suffered in Week 10.

The starting guard must clear the NFL's concussion protocol before he can return.

Jaylon Moore, OL, ankle

Jaylon Moore did not play in the win over the Jets on Sunday due to an ankle injury.

Noah Gray, TE, ribs

Noah Gray suffered a rib injury during Kansas City's game Sunday.

He was listed as questionable to return but did not re-enter the game.

"Noah Gray got hit in the ribs," Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said after the game. "We'll just see how he does.

Ben VanSumeren, FB, knee

Ben VanSumeren suffered a knee injury during Sunday's game and was ruled out.

The injury occurred on the same play as Gray's.

Reid said VanSumeren "tweaked his knee" but did not provide further details about its severity.

Omarr Norman-Lott, DT, knee

Omarr Norman-Lott was inactive after being listed as questionable entering Sunday's game.

Peter Woods, DL, neck

Peter Woods was listed as questionable and did not play Sunday.

text:
By Field Level Media

Nov 23 (Field Level Media) – Amid a lost season, the Los Angeles Chargers took another blow Sunday when Justin Herbert entered NFL concussion protocol after a 27-24 loss to the visiting New York Jets.

Herbert played the entire game for Los Angeles, but a member of the Chargers’ public relations team announced postgame that Herbert would not be available to the media because ​he had entered the protocol.

Herbert was 15 of 21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns against New York. He also ran eight ‌times for 32 yards and another touchdown.

But the franchise quarterback took six more sacks to bring his season total to 39, a league high.

Herbert previously suffered an injury to the middle finger of his left (non- throwing) hand earlier this month, but it wasn’t fractured and he was able to play through it.

If Herbert does not clear the protocol in time for the Chargers’ Week 12 home game against the New England Patriots on Nov. 29, DJ Uiagalelei would be in line to start under center. Los Angeles is 1-9, tied with ‌Tennessee and ​Miami for the worst record in the league.

–Ravens star running back Derrick Henry left Baltimore’s game against ⁠the Carolina Panthers in the fourth quarter to ⁠be evaluated for a head injury, but he said postgame that he felt fine.

“I’m good,” he told reporters in the locker room. “Bell just rung a little bit.”

Henry finished the game with 13 carries for 94 yards and a touchdown, adding four receptions for 17 yards. The Ravens, though, fell 35-33 to the Panthers for their sixth straight loss.

–The Jacksonville Jaguars left their 23-18 loss to the New York Giants with injury ​concerns for left tackle Walker Little, running back Bhayshul Tuten and cornerback Jarrian Jones.

Little suffered a knee injury and Jones hurt his chest. Neither returned to the game.

As for Tuten, he carried the ball on the Jaguars’ first play from scrimmage, and once he was tackled, he headed for the sideline. ⁠Tuten was in and out for the rest of the game as he continues to ⁠play through an ankle/foot injury that has hindered him since Nov. 1.

Tuten led the Jaguars in rushing with 33 ​yards on 10 attempts. He also caught three passes for 20 yards.

Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II picked up an ankle injury on the first defensive series ​and was ruled out.

–Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Alex Highsmith had a great game brewing before it was spoiled by an ankle ‌injury.

Highsmith recorded two sacks in his first six snaps against the Eagles, including a forced fumble recovered by Philadelphia, but on the latter sack it appeared he was rolled up on.

He was deemed questionable to return before being downgraded to out.

“Alex, (I) can’t say enough about him,” coach Mike McCarthy said postgame. “I mean, you just talk about his level of energy and professionalism, and so we’ll see what this brings. But yeah, I don’t really have a diagnosis for you on ⁠the ankle.”

Highsmith, who had 9.5 sacks a season ago, raised his season total to 5.5 before the injury.

In the same game, the Eagles lost cornerback Quinyon Mitchell to a hamstring injury. Philadelphia held on to win 19-16.

–San Francisco starting right tackle Colton McKivitz was carted off the field with a left leg ⁠injury in the game against the Minnesota Vikings on ‌Sunday night in Mexico City.

–Both the Detroit Lions and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers saw cornerbacks injured in their ⁠game.

Khalil Dorsey injured his wrist in the first quarter and was listed as questionable before returning to the ​game, which the ‌Lions won 31-21 to improve to 8-2. The Buccaneers ruled out Jacob Parrish after he sustained a ​back injury. Cornerback ⁠Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) and defensive lineman Elijah Simmons (concussion) also were hurt during the contest.

–Chicago Bears running back Roschon Johnson has an ankle injury that could keep him out of the Thanksgiving Day showdown against Detroit. Johnson, who has 103 rushing yards and one touchdown on 29 carries this season, didn’t record any stats before his exit following kickoff coverage in the first quarter of Chicago’s 21-13 win over New Orleans. Saints tight end Juwan Johnson (hamstring) was injured during the game.

–Arizona Cardinals linebacker Cody Simon picked up a calf injury and did not return to the team’s 34-7 loss to Kansas City. For the Chiefs, tight end Noah Gray (rib) and ​fullback Ben VanSumeren (knee) were injured.

(–Field Level Media)

text:
The San Francisco 49ers have been dealt a devastating injury blow with right tackle Colton McKivitz in the first half of the Week 11 game against the Minnesota Vikings.

The injury occurred in the second quarter of the contest, and it was immediately clear that the 49ers offensive lineman suffered a gruesome ankle injury.

McKivitz’s leg got trapped under another player. You can check out video of the aftermath of the play right here, but warning, it is hard to watch.

MORE: DK Metcalf facing suspension after Week 11 ejection vs. Eagles

McKivitz stayed down on the field after the play. Training staff tended to him before carting him off the field.

Players on both teams were obviously distraught at the site of McKivitz’s gruesome leg injury that will keep him out for the rest of the season.

The good news is McKivitz was alert while leaving the field in the cart. That doesn’t change just how awful it was to see him get injured.

MORE: Dak Prescott makes Cowboys history in dominant win over Titans

The loss is a tough one for the Niners. McKivitz is one of the team’s best offensive linemen and one of the best right tackles in the sport.

Entering Week 11, McKivitz was having a phenomenal season with Pro Football Focus grades of 82.8 overall, 71 in pass-blocking and 88.8 in run-blocking, ranking seventh, 37th and second among tackles in the NFL.

McKivitz didn’t allow a single sack and permitted just 12 pressures in 317 pass-blocking snaps.

Vederian Lowe is the next man up for San Francisco. He will present a significant downgrade for the Niners’ offense.

49ers’ injury woes continue

No team in the NFL has been as ravaged by injuries as San Francisco this season.

Going into the Sunday night game against the Vikings, the 49ers had a whopping 14 players on injured reserve. McKivitz will unfortunately be No. 15.

Despite all of their injuries, the Niners have been one of the best teams in the NFL this season.

Considering everything the Niners have had to overcome, there’s no question head coach Kyle Shanahan is one of the top candidates for NFL Coach of the Year.

text:
The Los Angeles Chargers had only a short time to enjoy their win over the Baltimore Ravens; that joy faded as they suffered a 27-24 loss to the New York Jets on Sunday. Their terrible season also took a worrying turn when star quarterback Justin Herbert was placed in the NFL's concussion protocol after the game.

Despite taking several hard hits throughout the contest, Herbert remained on the field until the final whistle, but the Chargers confirmed afterward that he had entered concussion protocol. They did not disclose when or how he sustained the injury, but the news immediately raised concerns about his situation, prompting reactions from fans.

Chargers Fans React to Justin Herbert's Concussion Scare

Herbert completed 15 of 21 passes for 131 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets while also contributing 32 rushing yards on eight attempts, including a rushing touchdown. He ranks No. 32 in PFN QB Impact with a grade of 62.5 through Week 11.

More than Herbert's performance, fans were more concerned about him entering the concussion protocol and called for the Chargers to shut him down rather than risk further damage.

"Damn they should shut him down for the rest of the season," one said.

"Sit him out and tank for JS (Jeremiah Smith)!" a fan said.

"SIT HIM. FOR THE LOVE OF GOD," one wrote.

"Just sit out for the year, Herbert," one added.

Herbert was sacked six times and absorbed eight quarterback hits in Sunday's game, including a facemask hit from Jets defensive end David Bailey. He has now been sacked 39 times through 10 games, the highest total among NFL quarterbacks this season.

SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN's Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer

According to ESPN Research, Herbert entered Sunday's game as the fourth-most pressured quarterback in the NFL, facing pressure on 41% of his dropbacks. The difference in his performance under pressure was also noticeable, as he completed all six of his passes when given a clean pocket but went 0-for-3 with two sacks when pressured in the first half.

That is why some directed their frustration toward the Chargers' front office and its handling of the offensive line.

"The Chargers front office's decision to cheap out on Justin Herbert's protection is why he's been literally abused the last 2 years and is now in concussion protocol," David Droegemeier, host of the "Locked On Chargers" podcast, wrote.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

"If I was Justin, I pull a Joe Burrow and make the front office take his health seriously with their wallets or threaten to request a trade or go the Andrew Luck route. This CAN NOT CONTINUE!! It's gross negligence,"

By Field Level Media

Nov 23 (Field Level Media) – Amid a lost season, the Los Angeles Chargers took another blow Sunday when Justin Herbert entered NFL concussion protocol after a 27-24 loss to the visiting New York Jets.

Herbert played the entire game for Los Angeles, but a member of the Chargers’ public relations team announced postgame that Herbert would not be available to the media because he had entered the protocol.

Herbert was 15 of 21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns ​against New York. He also ran eight times for 32 yards and another touchdown.

But the franchise quarterback took six more sacks to bring his season total to ‌39, a league high.

Herbert previously suffered an injury to the middle finger of his left (non- throwing) hand earlier this month, but it wasn’t fractured and he was able to play through it.

If Herbert does not clear the protocol in time for the Chargers’ Week 12 home game against the New England Patriots on Nov. 29, DJ Uiagalelei would be in line to start under center. Los Angeles is 1-9, tied with Tennessee and Miami for the worst record in the league.

–San Francisco starting right tackle Colton McKivitz was carted off the field with a left leg injury in the second quarter of the 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday night ‌in Mexico ​City. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said afterward that McKivitz sustained a fractured and dislocated left ankle and will miss the ⁠rest of the season.

He was blocking for running back Christian ⁠McCaffrey and was rolled up in a pile as McCaffrey was tackled.

“That was really crushing,” Shanahan said. “Colton’s had an unbelievable year.”

McKivitz, 30, has started every regular-season and playoff game since the 2023 season. He had played in 100% of the offensive snaps (563) through nine games this season and in 17 regular-season games in 2025 (1,117 snaps).

San Francisco selected him in the fifth round of the 2020 NFL Draft out of West Virginia. He played in 28 games (five starts) his first three seasons and a total of 88 regular-season games (65 ​starts) and 10 playoff games (five starts) in his seven-year career.

Vederian Lowe replaced McKivitz at right tackle on Sunday night.

For Minnesota, starting left tackle Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) exited the game briefly during the first half and then came out in the fourth quarter.

–Ravens star running back Derrick Henry left Baltimore’s game against the Carolina Panthers in the fourth quarter to be evaluated for a ⁠head injury, but he said postgame that he felt fine.

“I’m good,” he told reporters in the locker room. “Bell ⁠just rung a little bit.”

Henry finished the game with 13 carries for 94 yards and a touchdown, adding four receptions for 17 yards. The ​Ravens, though, fell 35-33 to the Panthers for their sixth straight loss.

–The Jacksonville Jaguars left their 23-18 loss to the New York Giants with injury concerns for left tackle Walker Little, running ​back Bhayshul Tuten and cornerback Jarrian Jones.

Little suffered a knee injury and Jones hurt his chest. Neither returned to the game.

As for Tuten, he ‌carried the ball on the Jaguars’ first play from scrimmage, and once he was tackled, he headed for the sideline. Tuten was in and out for the rest of the game as he continues to play through an ankle/foot injury that has hindered him since Nov. 1.

Tuten led the Jaguars in rushing with 33 yards on 10 attempts. He also caught three passes for 20 yards.

Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II picked up an ankle injury on the first defensive series and was ruled out.

–Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Alex Highsmith had a great game brewing before it was spoiled by an ⁠ankle injury.

Highsmith recorded two sacks in his first six snaps against the Eagles, including a forced fumble recovered by Philadelphia, but on the latter sack it appeared he was rolled up on.

He was deemed questionable to return before being downgraded to out.

“Alex, (I) can’t say enough about him,” coach Mike McCarthy said postgame. “I mean, you just talk about his level of energy and ⁠professionalism, and so we’ll see what this brings. But yeah, I don’t ‌really have a diagnosis for you on the ankle.”

Highsmith, who had 9.5 sacks a season ago, raised his season total to 5.5 ⁠before the injury.

In the same game, the Eagles lost cornerback Quinyon Mitchell to a hamstring injury. Philadelphia held on to win 19-16.

–Both ​the Detroit Lions ‌and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers saw cornerbacks injured in their game.

Khalil Dorsey injured his wrist in the first quarter and was listed ​as questionable before ⁠returning to the game, which the Lions won 31-21 to improve to 8-2. The Buccaneers ruled out Jacob Parrish after he sustained a back injury. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) and defensive lineman Elijah Simmons (concussion) also were hurt during the contest.

–Chicago Bears running back Roschon Johnson has an ankle injury that could keep him out of the Thanksgiving Day showdown against Detroit. Johnson, who has 103 rushing yards and one touchdown on 29 carries this season, didn’t record any stats before his exit following kickoff coverage in the first quarter of Chicago’s 21-13 win over New Orleans. Saints tight end Juwan Johnson (hamstring) was injured during the game.

–Arizona Cardinals linebacker Cody Simon picked up a calf injury and did not return to the team’s 34-7 loss to Kansas City. For the Chiefs, tight end Noah Gray (rib) ​and fullback Ben VanSumeren (knee) were injured.

(–Field Level Media)

text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are celebrating their 34-7 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, but that won’t last long. The team has to shift its focus quickly to the Buffalo Bills for a Week 12 game on Thanksgiving, with Kansas City and Buffalo meeting on “Thursday Night Football.”

Speaking to reporters after the Week 11 win over the Cardinals, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid gave his typical postgame injury update. The Chiefs suffered two injuries late in the game against Arizona.

Chiefs pick up two injuries late against the Cardinals

Chiefs FB Ben VanSumeren was ruled out with a knee injury. Meanwhile, TE Noah Gray was ruled questionable to return with a rib injury. Reid spoke briefly about both injuries after the game.

“As far as the injuries go, Noah Gray got hit in the ribs,” Reid said. “We’ll just see how he does. And then (Ben) VanSumeren tweaked his knee there. So, other than that, we came out pretty healthy.”

The problem with any injury on a short week is that players have that much less time to rest and prepare their bodies for the next game. That makes the injury status for both Gray and VanSumeren crucial to monitor when practice resumes. The Chiefs should hold at least an estimated practice on Monday, which will offer the first real look at where things stand.

Why the timing hurts Kansas City’s tight end room

These two injuries could be a massive blow to Kansas City at one specific position group. VanSumeren filled in this week as the Chiefs’ No. 4 tight end. That role opened up after TE Jared Wiley suffered a fractured ankle and landed on injured reserve this past week. After Wiley’s injury, the Chiefs signed TE John Fitzpatrick to the practice squad. They also have international player Thomas Odukoya on the practice squad at tight end.

The truth is, Kansas City simply doesn’t have much depth at tight end. Starter Travis Kelce is also playing through ankle and calf injuries. He’s a tough dude, and even Patrick Mahomes knows that it takes a lot to keep him off the football field.

“That’s Travis (Kelce),” Mahomes said. “I mean, you can’t take that dude off the football field. He loves it, and he goes out there and has success when he plays because he loves it that much. He competes. He’s gonna do whatever it takes to help the team win. And I mean, he made a couple big plays for us there, especially in the early part of the game. And that’s the type of leader he is. I’ll always say it makes my job as a quarterback easy. Like whenever you got a guy. That could take a game off, or could take practices off, or plays off, because he’s a Hall of Famer, and he’s the one that wants to get in there every single rep. That kind of gives you the mindset to tell the other guys, like, ‘Hey, like y’all want to take a rep off? Look at this guy.’ and it’s just easy for me as a leader to have someone like that on my team.”

Still, that leaves Jake Briningstool as the only fully healthy tight end on the 53-man roster. If either Gray or VanSumeren misses time, the Chiefs don’t have many options to lean on.

Chiefs have one emergency option at tight end

The good news is that Kansas City has WR Andrew Armstrong. He can line up in-line and play tight end if necessary. Armstrong also brings strength as a perimeter blocker, so the Chiefs can use him in that role if they find themselves in a pinch. However, the Chiefs will eventually have to address this injury situation at tight end. It might not happen with the short week, but they’ve got to scour their options.

Fitzpatrick hasn’t even spent a full week with the team. If Kansas City has to rely on him in any capacity against Buffalo, that would be cause for concern. NFL teams have to roll with the punches, especially on a short week. Still, the past two weeks have done a number on the Chiefs’ tight end room, and Monday’s practice estimation should reveal how much of a patchwork group Kansas City will bring to the Bills game.

The 49ers are all too familiar with the kind of ankle injury Colton McKivitz suffered in their 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday at Estadio Banorte.

Coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed the injury is a broken and dislocated left ankle. Linebacker Fred Warner suffered the same injury last season, and defensive tackle Gracen Halton's rookie season was cut short by the injury just two weeks ago.

"We think it’s broken and dislocated, similar to probably Fred’s last year, so that was really crushing," Shanahan told reporters after the game. "Colton’s had an unbelievable year. We care about all our guys, but it was tough to see Colton go down like that."

The crowd noise in Mexico City fell to a hush and 49ers players were distraught as the starting right tackle was carted off in the second quarter, after his left leg was stuck under multiple players at the end of a Christian McCaffrey run. His ankle was facing the wrong direction when the pile was off of him.

McKivitz had started 100 percent of the 49ers' offensive snaps this season and entered Week 11 with the longest active consecutive streak of snaps (270) without allowing a QB hit among tackles, per PFF.

San Francisco 49ers

But Shanahan is confident backup swing tackle Vedarian Lowe, who entered the game in McKivitz's absence, can fill the void moving forward.

"That’s why we brought Vederian here," Shanahan said. "He’s played a lot of football, and he stepped up really big in that game. He’s going to continue to do that the rest of this year for us."

title: 49ers' Colton McKivitz suffers season-ending ankle injury - ESPN
authors: Nick Wagoner, Anthony Gharib, Kevin Seifert, Matt Bowen, Tristan H. Cockcroft, ESPN Fantasy, Seth Walder, Todd Archer, Mike Kaye, Courtney Cronin
description:
Niners right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered what is believed to be a fractured and dislocated left ankle, an injury that will almost certainly end his season with seven regular-season games left.
McKivitz suffered the injury midway through the second quarter on what appeared to be a simple running play for Christian McCaffrey.
As Vikings linebacker Ivan Pace Jr. tackled McCaffrey, they appeared to roll into the back of McKivitz's left leg and ankle.
McKivitz tried to pry his leg loose, but his ankle bent in the opposite direction, a gruesome injury that NBC declined to show on the broadcast.
49ers left tackle Trent Williams immediately slammed his helmet in frustration after the injury, and multiple players immediately signaled for help from the sideline.
text:
MEXICO CITY -- The San Francisco 49ers left Mexico City with a big win against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday night but also lost a key offensive lineman.

Niners right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered what is believed to be a fractured and dislocated left ankle, an injury that will almost certainly end his season with seven regular-season games left.

"We think it's broken and dislocated, similar probably to Fred [Warner]'s last year," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "That was really crushing. Colton has had an unbelievable year. ... It was tough to see Colton go down like that."

McKivitz suffered the injury midway through the second quarter on what appeared to be a simple running play for Christian McCaffrey.

On first-and-10 at the Niners' 35, McCaffrey cut back to the right side for a 4-yard gain. As Vikings linebacker Ivan Pace Jr. tackled McCaffrey, they appeared to roll into the back of McKivitz's left leg and ankle.

McKivitz tried to pry his leg loose, but his ankle bent in the opposite direction, a gruesome injury that NBC declined to show on the broadcast.

49ers left tackle Trent Williams immediately slammed his helmet in frustration after the injury, and multiple players immediately signaled for help from the sideline. Niners medical personnel rushed to the field as other teammates dropped to a knee to pray. Vikings linebacker Kyle Van Noy and cornerback James Pierre turned away and each took a knee.

An air cast was placed on McKivitz's left leg, and he was carted to the locker room after some encouraging words and hugs from teammates, including Williams and guard Dominick Puni.

McKivitz has been a mainstay for the Niners at right tackle, starting 61 consecutive games, including Sunday night. He also leads all qualified tackles in pass block win rate (93.3%) this season, according to ESPN Analytics/NFL Next Gen Stats

After the 35-10 win against the Vikings, the Niners expressed dismay at McKivitz's injury.

"It's brutal," McCaffrey said. "He's somebody that is one of the heart and souls of this team, a guy who shows up every day with the right attitude. He's the standard, and we're going to really miss him. We all love him. We're praying for him. It's one of the worst parts about this game is stuff like that, but we love him and we're going to play for him from here on out."

Wide receiver Mike Evans said the team badly wanted to score a touchdown for McKivitz after his injury, and Evans provided those points with a 4-yard touchdown catch seven plays later.

Veteran Vederian Lowe replaced McKivitz at right tackle. Shanahan indicated that the team will ask Lowe to handle those duties moving forward.

San Francisco signed Lowe to a two-year deal with a base value of $9.25 million in March to serve as its swing tackle. Lowe entered the league as a sixth-round pick by the Vikings in 2022. He spent one season there and three with the Patriots before joining the Niners.

Lowe has appeared in 56 career games, including 25 starts.

"That's why we brought Vederian here," Shanahan said. "He's played a lot of football, and he stepped up really big in that game and he's going to continue to do that for the rest of the year for us."

By Field Level Media

Nov 23 (Field Level Media) – Amid a lost season, the Los Angeles Chargers took another blow Sunday when Justin Herbert entered NFL concussion protocol after a 27-24 loss to the visiting New York Jets.

Herbert played the entire game for Los Angeles, but a member of the Chargers’ public relations team announced postgame that Herbert would not be available to the media because he had entered the protocol.

Herbert was 15 of 21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns against New York. He also ran eight times for 32 yards and another touchdown.

But the franchise quarterback took six more sacks to bring his season total to 39, a league high.

Herbert previously suffered an injury to the middle finger of his left (non- throwing) hand earlier this month, but it wasn’t fractured and he was able to play through it.

If Herbert does not clear the protocol in time for the Chargers’ Week 12 home game against the New England Patriots on Nov. 29, DJ Uiagalelei would be in line to start under center. Los Angeles is 1-9, tied with Tennessee and Miami for the worst record in the league.

-Ravens star running back Derrick Henry left Baltimore’s game against the Carolina Panthers in the fourth quarter to be evaluated for a head injury, but he said postgame that he felt fine.

“I’m good,” he told reporters in the locker room. “Bell just rung a little bit.”

Henry finished the game with 13 carries for 94 yards and a touchdown, adding four receptions for 17 yards. The Ravens, though, fell 35-33 to the Panthers for their sixth straight loss.

-The Jacksonville Jaguars left their 23-18 loss to the New York Giants with injury concerns for left tackle Walker Little, running back Bhayshul Tuten and cornerback Jarrian Jones.

Little suffered a knee injury and Jones hurt his chest. Neither returned to the game.

As for Tuten, he carried the ball on the Jaguars’ first play from scrimmage, and once he was tackled, he headed for the sideline. Tuten was in and out for the rest of the game as he continues to play through an ankle/foot injury that has hindered him since Nov. 1.

Tuten led the Jaguars in rushing with 33 yards on 10 attempts. He also caught three passes for 20 yards.

Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II picked up an ankle injury on the first defensive series and was ruled out.

-Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Alex Highsmith had a great game brewing before it was spoiled by an ankle injury.

Highsmith recorded two sacks in his first six snaps against the Eagles, including a forced fumble recovered by Philadelphia, but on the latter sack it appeared he was rolled up on.

He was deemed questionable to return before being downgraded to out.

“Alex, (I) can’t say enough about him,” coach Mike McCarthy said postgame. “I mean, you just talk about his level of energy and professionalism, and so we’ll see what this brings. But yeah, I don’t really have a diagnosis for you on the ankle.”

Highsmith, who had 9.5 sacks a season ago, raised his season total to 5.5 before the injury.

In the same game, the Eagles lost cornerback Quinyon Mitchell to a hamstring injury. Philadelphia held on to win 19-16.

-San Francisco starting right tackle Colton McKivitz was carted off the field with a left leg injury in the game against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday night in Mexico City.

-Both the Detroit Lions and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers saw cornerbacks injured in their game.

Khalil Dorsey injured his wrist in the first quarter and was listed as questionable before returning to the game, which the Lions won 31-21 to improve to 8-2. The Buccaneers ruled out Jacob Parrish after he sustained a back injury. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (hamstring) and defensive lineman Elijah Simmons (concussion) also were hurt during the contest.

-Chicago Bears running back Roschon Johnson has an ankle injury that could keep him out of the Thanksgiving Day showdown against Detroit. Johnson, who has 103 rushing yards and one touchdown on 29 carries this season, didn’t record any stats before his exit following kickoff coverage in the first quarter of Chicago’s 21-13 win over New Orleans. Saints tight end Juwan Johnson (hamstring) was injured during the game.

-Arizona Cardinals linebacker Cody Simon picked up a calf injury and did not return to the team’s 34-7 loss to Kansas City. For the Chiefs, tight end Noah Gray (rib) and fullback Ben VanSumeren (knee) were injured.

(-Field Level Media)

Bosa stirred controversy when he commented on the crowd the last time San Francisco played in Mexico City in 2022.

text:
What to Know

Programming note: Immediately after the Week 11 game ends, watch "49ers Postgame Live" on NBC Sports Bay Area or stream the show in the NBC Sports app for full reaction, analysis and interviews.

The San Francisco 49ers (8-1) play their second international game of the season in Week 11 as they take on the Minnesota Vikings (7-2) on "Sunday Night Football" at the newly renovated Estadio Banorte in Mexico City.

After beating the Dallas Cowboys in Week 10, the 49ers flew to Colorado Springs for a week of practice instead of returning to the Bay so that they could prepare for the elevation at Estadio Banorte, which sits 7,352 feet above sea level.

Wide receiver Mike Evans, who has missed the last three games with Achilles tendinitis, was listed as questionable Friday but is active against the Vikings. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck) will not play.

The 49ers on Saturday activated defensive tackle CJ West from injured reserve and released veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks.

Matt Maiocco listed his five 49ers players to watch as they face the NFL's top-ranked defense.

Follow this live blog for the latest score updates, game highlights, news and analysis from Estadio Banorte in Mexico City:

49ers' offense roaring vs. Vikings' vaunted defense in first half

So far, Kyle Shanahan is winning the battle against Brian Flores.

Here are a few stats from the 49ers' dominant first half against Minnesota's defense.

HALFTIME: 49ers 28, Vikings 10

After Will Reichard was just short on his 71-yard field-goal attempt to end the first half, the 49ers went back to their locker room with three-score lead.

Patrick Mahomes sends well wishes to Colton McKivitz after injury

No one knows the value of an offensive lineman like a quarterback.

After Patrick Mahomes watched 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz get carted off with a scary-looking lower leg injury in the second quarter, the Chiefs QB posted a message to the San Francisco starter.

Here's to hoping McKivitz isn't too seriously injured.

Ji'Ayir Brown records pick-six to extend 49ers lead to 28-10 in the first half

Following a Mike Evans touchdown catch, San Francisco's defense came up big on the next drive when defensive back Ji'Ayir Brown intercepted a Kirk Cousins pass and returned it for a touchdown, giving the 49ers a 28-10 lead with 1:59 left in the first half.

The 49ers scored with 2:09 left in the second quarter to take a 21-10 lead, but after the Vikings took over on offense, Brown intercepted the ball on the first play of the drive from scrimmage. His interception came after the Vikings were flagged for an illegal block on the kickoff.

Brown's interception is his first of the season. The defense allowed a touchdown late in the first quarter, but since then, Minnesota's offense has not been able to get much going.

Mike Evans snags spectacular one-handed TD catch, 49ers go up 21-10

After missing the last three games, Mike Evans is back in a big way, and is making highlight reel catches in his return.

The 49ers' offense continues to fire on all cylinders, this time driving down the field on an eight-play, 65-yard drive lasting only 4:39, capping it off with Evans' 4-yard touchdown reception from Brock Purdy.

Purdy put the ball in a place that only Evans would be able to make the grab, and did not disappoint his quarterback.

The 49ers now extend their lead to 21-10 with 2:09 left in the first half as they continue to keep showing why they are the team to beat in the NFC.

Colton McKivitz suffers gruesome left ankle injury late in second quarter

It appears the 49ers will be without their starting right tackle for a while, if not for the remainder of the season.

On first-and-10 from the San Francisco 35-yard line, McCaffrey rushed for 4 yards to the right side before Colton McKivitz was rolled up on in a group of 49ers and Vikings players, with his left ankle very clearly dislocating.

McKivitz was surrounded by distraught teammates as his left foot was put in an air cast and he was carted off the field.

Vikings close gap with 48-yard field goal, trail 14-13

The Vikings closed the gap with 6:48 left in the second quarter, capping a 12-play, 45-yard drive with a 47-yard field goal that made it 14-13.

It almost looked like the drive was going to end in a punt just five plays earlier, but Minnesota went for it on fourth-and-1 on their own 47-yard line and Aaron Jones grabbed the first down on a 5-yard run.

49ers regain lead on George Kittle's second touchdown of the game

The 49ers scored first, and the Vikings responded, to tie things up in Mexico City, but San Francisco's offense is not backing down. Brock Purdy found George Kittle for an 8-yard touchdown with 14:13 to go in the first half to give San Francisco a 14-7 lead. Eddy Piñeiro converted the extra point.

Kittle's touchdown was his second of the game, improving his total to seven on the season. The touchdown capped off a strong drive that included a 19-yard completion to Jordan Watkins and a 34-yard completion to Mike Evans.

Kittle has two catches for 25 yards and Purdy has 116 passing yards and two touchdown passes in the first half. The Vikings defense is the best in the league, but San Francisco is forcing them to dig deep.

Minnesota gets the ball back with a chance to respond. The 49ers have momentum on their side, and are hoping to keep things going and return to the Bay Area at 9-1.

END OF FIRST QUARTER: 49ERS 7, VIKINGS 7

Vikings answer back, Aaron Jones pounds in TD to tie game at 7-7

Kirk Cousins and the Vikings did not stay scoreless for long.

Justin Jefferson got the drive started with a 29-yard reception, getting the Vikings into 49ers' territory quick. As the drive continued, the running back tandem of Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason continued to pound the rock into the red zone.

Aaron Jones finished the efficient nine-play, 90-yard drive with a rushing score from 11 yards out, taking only 4:40 to tie the game up at 7-7.

The 49ers will look to respond after scoring on their opening drive of the game, now with 1:13 remaining in the opening quarter.

Should this have been roughing the passer penalty on Nick Bosa?

As he tries to claim his first sack of the season, Nick Bosa nearly had one in the first quarter before Kirk Cousins got the ball off.

But instead of a near-sack, Bosa was handed a roughing the passer penalty after he couldn't avoid falling on top of Cousins -- a call that was met by plenty of boos.

Was it justified?

Will Reichard misses 55-yard field-goal attempt on Vikings' first drive

Kirk Cousins and Minnesota's offense took over from their own 35-yard line, trailing 7-0 after San Francisco's opening-drive touchdown.

Cousins completed passes of 9 and 20 yards to Jauan Jennings and T.J. Hockenson, respectively, on the drive, while Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason rushed a combined three times for minus-1 yard.

Cousins' incomplete pass to Jennings on third-and-11 from the San Francisco 37-yard line forced a 55-yard Will Reichard field-goal attempt, which soared wide left, preserving the 49ers' 7-0 lead.

George Kittle passes Owens for second-most receiving yards in 49ers history

The People's Tight End is solidifying his case as one of the best pass-catchers in 49ers franchise history.

And he did it in style.

With his first reception, a 17-yard touchdown catch, against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday at Estadio Banorte, 49ers tight end George Kittle passed Pro Football Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for second-most receiving yards in franchise history.

Kittle trailed Owens, who finished his career in San Francisco with 8,572 receiving yards in 121 games played, by just 7 receiving yards.

George Kittle scores TD on opening drive; 49ers take 7-0 lead

Brock Purdy and the 49ers made quick work of the Vikings' vaunted defense on the game's opening drive, taking a 7-0 lead on a 17-yard touchdown pass to George Kittle with 11:16 left in the first quarter.

The touchdown completed a seven-play, 72-yard scoring drive and also put Kittle ahead of Terrell Owens for the second-most receiving yards in 49ers franchise history.

Purdy went 4-for-4 during the drive, and Mike Evans caught a 14-yard pass for a first down in his return from injury.

Fred Warner leads 49ers out while carrying Mexico flag

Fred Warner and the 49ers are in Mexico City, looking to beat the Vikings and truly separate themselves from the rest of the NFL. Warner is making sure that the Mexican fans are fully on their side.

Warner ran out of the tunnel carrying the Mexico flag, something he also did in 2022, the last time San Francisco played in Mexico City. Warner has Mexican heritage, and carrying the flag is a fitting way to acknowledge that part of his life.

Warner missed most of last season with an ankle injury, but is wasting no time returning to form. He has 88 total tackles, five forced fumbles and a fumble recovery in nine games.

The 49ers have Super Bowl aspirations, but if they want to get there, they need to beat teams like the Vikings. Can San Francisco return to the Bay Area on a three-game winning streak?

Are 49ers, Vikings in trouble with turf in Mexico City?

Both teams better be sure-footed tonight.

The turf at Estadio Banorte might not be on par with Levi's Stadium, as shared by NBC Sports Bay Area's Jennifer Lee Chan.

With Mike Evans recovering from Achilles tendinitis and Nick Bosa overcoming several past ACL injuries, this has to be a scary sight for San Francisco.

The 49ers fan poll results are in: Shannahan vs. Flores takes the stage

We asked, you answered. The votes are in. Shanahan vs. Flores looks to be the highlight of tonight's clash between two NFC juggernauts.

Leading up to Week 11, Brian Flores has coordinated the Vikings' defense to near-perfection. While Kyle Shanahan on the other side has turned the 49ers' offense into a well-oiled machine.

An immovable object will meet an unstoppable force tonight, and the fans agree it's what they are most looking forward to from this playoff-like matchup.

Why NFL extended length of halftime for Mexico City game

The NFL had to add six minutes to tonight's halftime thanks to an interesting feature at Estadio Banorte.

The mid-game break was extended so that both teams have enough time to make it back to the field, thanks to the stadium's exceptionally long tunnels from the locker rooms to the gridiron.

You never know what to expect in an international game.

Mike Tomlin breaks down Brock Purdy's tough challenge vs. Vikings

Brock Purdy is in the midst of an MVP-caliber season for the 49ers. This week, he faces the NFL's best defense in the Minnesota Vikings. The Vikings lead the league with a 78.6 percent blitz rate, which could force Purdy to adjust.

Former coach Mike Tomlin broke down keys to the game for San Francisco and how to overcome Minnesota's extreme blitz tendencies. He compared the Vikings' scheme to what the Rams franchise ran during their 2001 Super Bowl berth season.

The 49ers have struggled against the Vikings in recent seasons. Their last win against them came at home in Week 12 of the 2021 NFL season. San Francisco lost the 2023 and 2024 matchups in Minnesota.

San Francisco is 8-1 and looking to win its third straight game. Can the 49ers gain an even greater advantage towards earning the No. 1 seed in the NFC?

49ers Faithful arrive in Mexico City, look ready to take over SNF

The Faithful are showing up in full force ahead of tonight's NFC juggernaut matchup against the Vikings, looking to make sure their sea of red is an overwhelming force.

Do the 49ers have the strongest global fanbase? After Week 1 in Australia, and now tonight in Mexico City, it is starting to seem that way.

Greenlaw inactive for 49ers in Week 11 game vs. Vikings

The 49ers will be without one of their key defensive players for their "Sunday Night Football" clash with the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw is one of five inactive San Francisco players.

As NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco mentioned, wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) is active and will play after missing the team's past three games.

Nick Bosa booed by fans ahead of ‘Sunday Night Football' clash vs. Vikings

The 49ers have a large following of fans below the border, and they made their presence known esrly tonight.

Nick Bosa is the one 49ers player who might not be well received. Bosa was booed when he took the field for pregame warmups after he made comments about Mexican fans at a midweek press conference.

Bosa stirred controversy when he commented on the crowd the last time San Francisco played in Mexico City in 2022. He said the crowd was loud but criticized them for chanting the whole time like they do in soccer, suggesting that they need information on when to cheer.

Bosa's comments were not well received, but he is not focused on the repercussions. Instead, he is still in search of his first sack of the season and is eager to help the 49ers' defense stop a revamped Vikings offense.

George Kittle, Aaron Jones arrive to stadium with Mexico City flair

George Kittle and Aaron Jones brought some Mexican culture to their pregame outfits.

The 49ers tight end, who is a huge pro wrestling fan, arrived to Estadio Banorta in a luchador mask -- specifically that of Pénta, who is from Mexico City and is both a fan and friend of Kittle.

On the other side of tonight's matchup, Vikings running back Aaron Jones donned a classic mariachi suit.

49ers face fascinating roster decision for game vs. Vikings

With the banged-up 49ers getting healthier at wide receiver, it created quite the conundrum for coach Kyle Shanahan: Who returns punts against the Vikings?

As NBC Sports Bay Area's 49ers insider Matt Maiocco notes, San Francisco rarely carries six active wide receivers on gameday. But if Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Keenan Allen, Jordan Watkins and Demarcus Robinson all are active, the 49ers might need a sixth wideout to handle punts.

Jacob Cowing would be the obvious choice to return punts.

Fred Warner reflects on ‘magnitude' of representing heritage in Mexico City game

As Fred Warner and the 49ers return to Mexico City on Sunday, their matchup against the Minnesota Vikings holds extra meaning for San Francisco's star linebacker.

Warner had the stadium roaring before the 49ers' game at Estadio Banorte, then known as Estadio Azteca, back in 2022 when he ran onto the field waving the Mexican flag, taking the field in the country where his grandfather was born for the first time as an NFL star.

The moment quickly went viral, and Warner recently told ESPN's Nick Wagoner he gets goosebumps every time he sees it.

"I don't think I understood the magnitude of the moment," Warner told Wagoner on Thursday. "Being in Mexico in front of the fans, really representing them and representing that part of me and my family was bigger than I even thought."

Dan Orlovsky picks 49ers player who puts ‘fear of God' in Brian Flores, Vikings

Sunday's marquee game between the 49ers and Minnesota Vikings has been billed as a matchup between arguably the two best play-callers on their respective sides of the ball.

San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan's offense leads the NFL in yards per game and is second in points per game. On the other hand, Minnesota defensive coordinator Brian Flores' unit leads the league in points allowed per game and is second in yards allowed per game.

But ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky doesn't believe Shanahan is the primary key to this weekend's game for the 49ers. Instead, he explained why running back Christian McCaffrey could give San Francisco the edge.

"I think San Francisco has the ultimate chess piece: McCaffrey," Orlovsky said Friday on "First Take." "This is a McCaffrey versus Flores game for me. It's not a Shanny versus Flores game. Two 49ers safeties fined after win vs. Cowboys, but Malik Mustapha not punished

Sigle was fined $6,142 for what the NFL determined was a hit on a defenseless player. Sigle’s play in defense against Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb on a second-quarter incomplete pass was not penalized at the time.

Neal was fined $8,639 for his fourth-quarter facemask penalty against Cowboys return specialist KaVontae Turpin.

Why 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan wasn't surprised by viral Mac Jones Bumpboxx video

Kyle Shanahan, speaking with NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco on "49ers Game Plan," laid out how the 49ers' cornerbacks can mount a bounce-back performance against the Minnesota Vikings and their strong receiving corps.

Five vital 49ers to watch vs. Vikings in Mexico City as NFC powerhouses collide

But what makes it stand out even more is the element of strength vs. strength. The 49ers own one of the NFL's top offenses, while the Vikings are led by an aggressive and productive defense.

"It was amazing," Piñeiro told NBC Sports Bay Area's Kylen Mills. "I would even say not so much for the money, but just kind of (being) somewhere where they believe in me and they trust in me, and being on a team. Purdy got the opportunity to reminisce about his relationship with Jennings during a press conference Thursday, where he was asked what his favorite memory was with his old teammate.

"Man, there's a lot," Purdy said. "Super Bowl, him balling out, throwing a touchdown pass on a trick play, catching a touchdown pass. 49ers rookie RB Kaelon Black manifested being drafted into the NFL by a Shanahan

Kaelon Black is having a strong debut season for the 49ers, leading all rookie running backs in rushing and proving to be a strong complement to Christian McCaffrey.

San Francisco found a gem in Black, selecting him in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft after he won a national championship at Indiana. As it turns out, his arrival in the Bay Area aligns with the destiny he wished for himself. Kind of.

Black went on "Good Morning Football" on Thursday and talked about his journey to the league, revealing that when he was a kid, he wrote a book manifesting playing in the NFL after being drafted by a Shanahan.

“It’s funny because I did,” Black told host Jamie Erdahl. “I was probably in like fourth grade in Washington at the time, and at the time, Mike Shanahan was the coach and I was saying, like ‘I’m going to be the first overall pick drafted by Mike Shanahan. As 49ers train at altitude, ex-Patriots safety Devin McCourty explains benefits

AIR FORCE ACADEMY, Colo. — The 49ers are on their second extended trip of the 2026 NFL season, and coach Kyle Shanahan is confident that the extra effort again will help them on the field.

The 49ers traveled straight to Colorado Springs after their Week 9 win in Dallas to train at the Air Force Academy, whose practice fields sit at 7,258 feet above sea level, to prepare for Mexico City's elevation (7,350 ft.).

“I think that’s just science, which I don’t know much about, but I just know from personal experience growing up here,” Shanahan said on Wednesday. “I think it all does help. It’s not everything either. It’s just like when you come to play Denver. I always think the Broncos have a two-percent advantage every time at home because they’re just more used to it.

“Two percent doesn’t win you games, but it’s definitely nicer to play in something when you’re acclimated to that altitude and stuff so you’re not as out of breath. It’s rarely the difference in winning and losing, but anything that helps, if it works for our team, we try to do it.”

San Francisco boasts the second-best scoring offense in the NFL, while Minnesota's defense is the best scoring defense.

Kyle Shanahan, the 49ers' coach and offensive play-caller, will be put to the test against Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores. And if there is one thing a Flores-led defense will do, it's turning up the heat by blitzing.

"[Flores] is more unique than all the other 31 guys," Shanahan told reporters Wednesday. "He's the one guy who commits to this and it's not just a fad for these nine games or whatever. He's been doing it his whole time in Minnesota. He did the same thing in Miami.

Jake Brendel, 49ers offense face extreme test against unique Vikings defense

AIR FORCE ACADEMY, Colo. — Jake Brendel, midway through his fifth season as the 49ers’ starting center, might face the biggest challenge of his career on Sunday night.

And it will be just as much mental as it is physical.

While all eyes will be on 49ers quarterback on how he handles the pressure of the Minnesota Vikings’ defense. All ears along the team’s offensive line will be tuned to the communication from Brendel.

“Across the league, usually a defense kind of specializes in one, two, maybe, three different things that they like to do,” Brendel said on "49ers Talk." “The Vikings and Brian Flores kind of throw the whole kitchen sink at you.”

49ers' Nick Bosa has request of Mexico City fans for Week 11 game vs. Vikings

Nick Bosa has one request for the passionate 49ers fans in Mexico City attending Sunday's game vs. the Minnesota Vikings.

Speaking to reporters after practice on Wednesday, San Francisco's defensive end was asked about the support the team received during their game against the Arizona Cardinals four years ago in Mexico City, and while recalling how loud the crowd was, had a request for the international 49ers fans in attendance.

"Yeah, I kind of want ... I think we need some information given to the fans so they know when to cheer," Bosa said. "Because they just chant the whole time. If we can kind of teach them, no offense to them and their soccer cheering techniques, but if they can cheer when we're on defense, that would be great."

The crowd for that 2022 game at Estadio Azteca, now named Estadio Banorte, was overwhelmingly 49ers fans, and that likely will be the case again on Sunday against the Vikings.

49ers star Nick Bosa makes honest admission about his slow start to the season

AIR FORCE ACADEMY, Colo. — According to Nick Bosa, the All-Pro is not playing his best football, at least not yet.

The star pass rusher has not logged a quarterback sack in four games, which is the longest drought in his NFL career. But now it’s about more than just stats for Bosa, who spoke to the media on Wednesday.

“I think at this point in my career it’s a lot easier,” Bosa said about the lack of numbers on the stat sheet. “In the past when I was younger it would eat at me a lot more, just strictly the stat aspect. Brandon Aiyuk reportedly recently reconciled with Commanders QB Jayden Daniels

Brandon Aiyuk is nearing a return to the NFL after his reinstatement earlier this month. But it won't be with the 49ers.

San Francisco received a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk on Nov. 9, meaning that he does not count towards the 53-man roster and is not paid. The exemption expires on Nov. 23, when the team likely will release their former first-round pick.

Aiyuk's playing future remains uncertain, but the one team that has been connected to him the most has been the Washington Commanders. Aiyuk has a long-standing relationship with Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels that soured this offseason, when he took social media shots at him and his mother.

The jabs seemed to put an end to any speculation that he would join the Commanders upon his reinstatement, but the two since have made-up after Aiyuk reached out to Daniels to hash things out, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported in a recent story.

Kyle Shanahan downplays edge 49ers might have in second matchup vs. Kirk Cousins

The 49ers defense will see Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins for the second time in three weeks on Sunday in Mexico City.

Cousins played his last game with the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 9 against the 49ers in Santa Clara, in which San Francisco came away with a 38-17 win. Cousins subsequently was traded to Minnesota ahead of the NFL trade deadline one week ago.

Despite the fact that the 49ers recently saw the same quarterback they will face Sunday, coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters Wednesday that he does not believe it provides his team with an advantage.

"I don't think it matters. It might matter for some individuals, maybe just something they picked up or something like that..." Shanahan explained. "... But Kirk plays very consistently no matter what team he's on. He's going to run the scheme of that team and do it at a high level. He did that with the Raiders. He's done it in one week with Minnesota, and I know that will continue."

Rich Eisen makes the case for 49ers holding WR Mike Evans out vs. Vikings

The 49ers could get star wide receiver Mike Evans back as soon as this week, but there is one person who is not ready to see the future Hall of Famer return.

ESPN's Rich Eisen spoke on his show, "The Rich Eisen Show" on Tuesday and gave his take on Evans' return from Achilles tendonitis, with Eisen suggesting the team continues to rest him so that he does not make things worse.

“This guy who’s got Achilles issues, amongst many others, do you want to put him on foreign turf, literally and figuratively?,” Eisen said. “You want to do that? You want to put him on the field in Mexico City? I have no idea… I’d hold him out. But then, how long do you hold him out? Because two weeks after that, you know where the 49ers are? The place they do not want to go.

“They don’t want to go to MetLife [Stadium]... everybody talks about the substation. That’s not real. You know what’s real? That MetLife turf. So maybe what you do is you sit him and then you’ve got to play him at home against Seattle. Then he sits out against the Giants ... maybe you sit him in Mexico, you play him at home then you sit him at the Giants, and then everybody’s healthy, and let’s go on the rest of the way now.”

49ers receive NFL's ‘best team' praise from Kevin O'Connell before Week 11 game

The 49ers are 8-1 to begin the 2026 NFL season, their best start since 2019.

But things are about to get a lot more difficult. After beating the Dallas Cowboys, the 49ers shift their focus to a pivotal matchup against the 7-2 Minnesota Vikings, the league's best defense.

The 49ers have plenty of star power on offense, though and could use this game as an opportunity to truly separate themselves in the NFC.

Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell spoke to reporters on Monday and praised the 49ers while looking ahead to the Week 11 "Sunday Night Football" showdown in Mexico City.

Mike Evans misses Wednesday 49ers practice, still has chance to play vs. Vikings

AIR FORCE ACADEMY, Colo. — Wide receiver Mike Evans made the trip to join after the team’s Week 10 game against the Dallas Cowboys.

But Evans will not practice on Wednesday, as the 49ers begin their preparations to face the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday in Mexico City.

Wild stat shows 49ers' offense vs. Vikings' defense could be all-time NFL clash

Entering Week 11, the 49ers have the second-best scoring offense, and the Minnesota Vikings boast the best scoring defense in the NFL.

Only one side can win when the two teams face off Sunday in Mexico City.

The matchup between such a potent offense and shutdown defense is a rare one in NFL history this late into the season. title: Justin Herbert Injured, Latest Updates as Chargers QB Enters Concussion Protocol After Loss to Jets
description:
Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert entered the NFL's concussion protocol after Sunday's 27-24 loss to the New York Jets.
Herbert went 15-of-21 for 131 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions.

text:
Whether Jameson Williams is carefree or careless is in the eye of the beholder.

One thing he is exceptional at is football, and while he gave Lions fans plenty to celebrate on Sunday, he probably scared the hell out of them, too.

The dynamic wide receiver hauled in a 57-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff during the third quarter against the Buccaneers, flashing his burning speed in the process.

But to cross the goalline, Williams front flipped into the endzone, and didn’t exactly stick the landing.

The acrobatic celebration immediately drew anxious reactions from Lions fans, as well as the broadcast, who watched star defensive lineman Aidan Hutchinson suffer a season-ending torn ACL while celebrating a sack just one week earlier.

“Didn’t hutch just blow out his knee for the season over celebrating ???” one fan wrote under ESPN’s post of the touchdown. “You’d think Dan would tell them to chill on the excessive celebrations.”

“Guarantee you every Lions fans heart stopped for a second on that landing,” another fan wrote.

“Jameson has no sense of the situation. He’s so funny,” Barstool’s Liam Blutman added.

The USA Today affiliate Lions Wire posted, “And every Lions fan had a temporary panic attack.”

The Detroit Times posted, “NEVER DO THIS AGAIN JAMO 💀💀💀” in reacting to the touchdown.

Hutchinson’s injury came during Detroit’s 35-10 victory over the Patriots in Munich, Germany on Nov. 15.

After sacking quarterback Drake Maye, who also exited early with an ankle injury, Hutchinson jumped into the air, pumping his fist, and landed awkwardly on his right leg, tearing his ACL and ending his season.

The injury deprived Detroit, a Super Bowl contender, of one of its most important defensive players for the rest of 2026 and into 2027.

“I honestly can’t believe it,” Hutchinson wrote on his Instagram once the severity of his injury was confirmed. “I’ve jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me.”

The Lions cruised to a 31-21 win over the Bucs, with Williams having recorded four catches for 93 yards and the now-infamous touchdown celebration.

text:
The Miami Dolphins will face the Buffalo Bills during today's game with the offensive line at full strength because of Aaron Brewer's return.

Brewer, a second-team All Pro in 2025, exhibited the NFL's concussion protocol on Saturday and returned to his starting center role.

Brewer missed last Sunday's fourth-quarter loss to the Indianapolis Colts because of the concussion he suffered the previous week. It was the second game he's missed since his Dolphins tenure began three years ago.

The Dolphins will be missing all three of the team's top defensive linemen - Zach Sieler, Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers - who each suffered season ending injuries this month. Kenneth Grant, Keith Cooper Jr., and Jordan Jefferson will be the defensive tackles responsible for stopping Bills tailback James Cook, who is having yet another Pro Bowl worthy season.

The Dolphins will also be playing the first game of the regular season without safety Dante Trader Jr., who has started all but one game this season. Trader missed practice all week nursing a shoulder and groin injury he's been battling most of the season.

Zayne Anderson, a four-year veteran who came with head coach Jeff Hafley from Green Bay, is expected to replace Trader as the safety paired with rookie Michael Taaffe.

Also inactive for Sunday's game was offensive linemen Caeden Wallace and Christian Haynes, tight end Justin Joly, receiver Jared Wayne, cornerback Jaylin Simpson and punter Bradley Pinion.

Pinion injured his groin last week and will be replaced by Jack Browning, who was signed to the practice squad this week to handle the punting and holding role.

The Dolphins will also have a new kicker this week after releasing Zane Gonzalez, who missed two field goals and an extra punt in last week's loss to the Colts, and replacing him with Daniel Carlson.

text:
After losing star receiver Puka Nacua to season-ending knee surgery, the Los Angeles Rams are reportedly set to get their other star wideout back in the lineup.

On Sunday's episode of NFL GameDay, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Rams veteran receiver Davante Adams had an "outside chance" to return from injured reserve for Wednesday's matchup against the Green Bay Packers, but that is "not gonna happen," and he is more likely to be activated around mid-December.

Adams underwent a procedure to repair a ruptured hamstring suffered in the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6. He was initially given a return timeline of six to 10 weeks.

Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters earlier this month that the team opted not to acquire a wide receiver at the trade deadline because he was "optimistic" that Adams would return from his hamstring injury "sooner than later." Nacua hadn't been ruled out for the season at the time, but in retrospect, the team would've benefited from another addition.

Rapoport reported that Nacua "was trying to get back from a significant MCL injury," but "was not able to do it without surgery." He underwent surgery on his MCL on Tuesday, but his PCL and turf toe were "untouched." The 25-year-old is facing a "four- to five-month recovery," ruling him out for the entire year even if the Rams advance to the Super Bowl. The 2026 season is the final year of his rookie contract, and his future in Los Angeles now appears uncertain.

The Rams are riding a four-game win streak into Wednesday's game against the Packers, and they will try to sustain their momentum until they can get Adams back onto the field.

text:
Brock Bowers is such a pivotal element to the Las Vegas Raiders offense, and you'd have to imagine even more so with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza set to make his second start. However, as Bowers has continued to battle an ankle injury, his status for the Raiders' matchup against the rival Denver Broncos on Sunday in Week 11 is a toss-up. That's even more worrisome for fantasy football managers considering that Vegas plays in the 4:25 p.m. ET window, making decisions about starting him that much more crucial for fantasy.

So let's check in on what to do with Bowers with the latest injury updates for the Raiders tight end, but also how both Vegas and fantasy managers will and should adjust if Bowers is unable to play on Sunday.

Is Brock Bowers playing on Sunday? Raiders TE a real game-time decision

Brock Bowers is truly a game-time decision for Sunday's matchup against the Broncos in Week 11. He didn't practice for the Raiders to start to week and then was limited on Thursday and Friday as well. That puts him truly living up to the questionable tag that he's been labeled with for this game and we probably won't know his availability until 1.5 hours before kickoff when inactives are released. With the late start, though, fantasy managers should consider the upside if he plays.

Last week, Bowers was also still limited with the ankle injury he's still battling, but he played only 11 snaps in that outing. That's important because we've seen that several times. When Bowers is playing at less than 100 percent, the team has shown no issues with limiting his usage and even his time on the field. When that's the case, he's no longer the must-start TE1, but rather more of a touchdown-dependent option.

While there is the chance that he could be fully good to go by kickoff and have his normal high workload for the Raiders in this offense, history tells us that Bowers being questionable likely limits his fantasy upside regardless of if he plays or not.

Raiders TE depth chart without Brock Bowers

The Raiders have one of the best overall tight end rooms in the NFL with Michael Mayer not just being the proverbial backup to Bowers, but also just being on the field often with Bowers being used as a big slot. Mayer is a startable option each week even when Bowers is healthy, and that continues to be the case even more strongly if Bowers is out or limited and playing.

That being said, Mayer was in that spot last week and garnered only two catches on three targets for 16 yards. There is far more upside there, but with a rookie quarterback in Mendoza, that does make things a little less certain for the veteran tight end. For that matter, though, Thomas is largely a non-factor.

Instead, we'll see Mayer and other players in the Raiders offense be the beneficiaries of Bowers' injury when it comes to fantasy.

Fantasy outlook for Raiders if Brock Bowers doesn't play

In his debut against a similarly dominant defense to the one the Raiders will see with Denver, Mendoza spread the ball around, especially with Vegas really unable to run the ball effectively. While I don't have high hopes for Ashton Jeanty as a runner against the Broncos, the fact that he led the team in receptions and receiving yards (four for 46 yards) last week makes him someone who will likely get a bump with Bowers either limited or out.

Beyond that, Jack Bech becomes an intriguing option to play at wide receiver with Bowers' injury given that he led the team in targets with seen last week. Jeanty and Jalen Nailor were next on that list with four targets apiece. While Bech only converted those chances into two catches for 10 yards, it's a potential deep-league flier worth taking given how much he was targeted.

And while Tre Tucker only got two targets that resulted in one catch for nine yards, his performance this season suggests that he's another flier-worthy player this week given that he has been inconsistent but primed for boom weeks pretty regularly.

text:
The Los Angeles Rams are coming out of their bye week with plenty of storylines as they prepare to take on the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday. While the Rams are riding a four-game winning streak, much of the conversation this week has centered around Puka Nacua and his season-ending injury. Let’s get into that and more in this week’s Sunday Morning Notebook.

Puka Nacua's Suspension and Surgery Spark Controversy

There’s no doubt that wide receiver Puka Nacua has been the topic of conversation this week. The Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve before he was suspended by the NFL, and then it was later announced that he had undergone season-ending surgery.

Nacua’s suspension came with a lot of controversy, especially with him also being on injured reserve. Even before Nacua underwent surgery and was ruled out for the season, his suspension wasn't expected to cost him any additional games beyond those he would already miss on injured reserve.

According to The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones, the suspension was reached via settlement between the NFL, NFLPA, and Nacu’a representation.

“Nacua accepted the league’s three-game punishment — which could be more accurately described as a three-game check forfeiture — and the league walked away with what it considers a precedent-setting victory, even if it’s not viewed that way on the outside,” said Jones.

Nacua’s surgery has also come with its share of controversy with some not believing that the team was fully on board with it. Even after the surgery was announced, it was thought that Nacua could possibly return for the playoffs with Sean McVay saying that he would be out a few months.

ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Sunday morning that three doctors recommended that Nacua undergo the procedure. Schefter also noted that the timeline is expected to be 4-5 months, which would put Nacua out for the remainder of the regular season and playoffs.

Kobie Turner, Justin Dedich Expected to Return Against Packers

While the Rams will be without Nacua for the remainder of the season, they are expected to get some reinforcements back from injured reserve starting Wednesday against the Green Bay Packers. The Rams have officially designated Kobie Turner for return and Justin Dedich will also be back.

“Unless there's something unforeseen that occurs, we'll have both those guys. They'll be up and ready to roll,” said McVay on Saturday.

Both players will provide a boost for the Rams. The Rams have missed Turner’s presence on the interior. If the Rams get Turner back on Wednesday, it will be the first time they’ll have him, Aaron Donald, and Myles Garrett on the field at the same time.

Additionally, Dedich will at least provide depth on the offensive line. It will be interesting to see if he starts at left guard in place of Steve Avila or if the Rams go with Bill Murray. Dedich could also potentially play at center in place of Coleman Shelton, but guard is more likely. Again, the Rams will at least get some much-needed depth on the interior of the offensive line with Dedich’s return.

Rams' Controversial Australia Travel Plans Could Have Lasting Impact

Earlier this season, the Rams took a lot of criticism for how they handled their travel plans to Australia. While the San Francisco 49ers arrived nearly a week before the game, the Rams arrived just over 24 hours before the game. During the week, the 49ers integrated with Australia’s culture and got involved in the community. That experience was part of what the Rams missed.

Over the past several years, the NFL has put a lot of time, effort, and money into the international games. The Rams not showing up until right before the game was almost a slap in the face to the league. They took a similar approach last year when they stayed for a week in Baltimore before traveling to London to play the Jacksonville Jaguars.

IThe league has discussed potentially requiring teams to spend a minimum number of nights in the host city before international games. That likely won’t go over well with some coaching staffs, but part of the NFL’s international initiative is for the teams to build a connection in the host city. The Rams have spent time previously in Australia, but showing up a day before the game doesn’t make the cost of travel worth it.

This is going to be something to monitor over the next few years and could potentially be a point of discussion in the next CBA.

text:
The Green Bay Packers will have their top defensive star back in action when they take the field at SoFi Stadium against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night.

Edge rusher Micah Parsons will make his season debut when the Packers take on the Rams, FOX Sports NFL insider Jay Glazer reported Sunday.

Parsons' return to game action will come nearly a full calendar year after he tore his ACL. He suffered the injury on Dec. 14 last season, going down on a non-contact play as he pressured Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix.

That injury led to a downturn for Green Bay last season. The Packers lost their final five games, including the game Parsons left early and their wild-card round loss to the Chicago Bears.

The Packers placed Parsons on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list to open this season, with the expectation being that he would return at some point in October or November. Parsons made his way back to the practice field on Nov. 4 and has been practicing for the past couple of weeks.

With Parsons taking nearly a full year to return from his ACL tear, Glazer pointed out that Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL and MCL on the same day as the Packers' star last season but was ready to play in Week 1 this season. The players took different approaches to their rehabs, with Mahomes taking the unconventional route to undergo surgery before the swelling in his knee subsided, while Parsons had his surgical repair after the swelling dissipated.

Glazer suggested that maybe Mahomes' approach might be the smarter way to approach rehabbing an ACL tear moving forward.

"This is zero indictment on Micah Parsons," Glazer said on "FOX NFL Kickoff." "I started asking other teams, ‘If this works for Mahomes, why would nobody else do it?’ Other teams just said, ‘We don’t do [that].' I'm like, ‘Why not?' And they just said, ‘We don’t do it.'

"I just think people need to call the Chiefs after this and say, ‘Whatever you did for Patrick Mahomes, let us know it because we’re going to start doing that as well.'"

Regardless, the Packers are getting a key player back at the right time. Green Bay's defense has been one of the better units in the league this season and ranks fourth in sacks (29). But Parsons is one of the best pass rushers in the game, logging at least 12 sacks in each of his first five NFL seasons.
